builder_plan.scenario: Your workload might fit a smaller or differently structured model.
builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: A KAN-based Non-linear Factorization for Embedding Layer Compression
summary: It replaces the purely linear low-rank decomposition of an embedding matrix with a factorization that inserts learnable univariate (KAN-style) nonlinear projections inside the compressed embedding layer, optionally initialized from a pretrained uncompressed embedding and refined with distillation. The cost is additional per-parameter compute for the learnable univariate functions, extra implementation complexity over a standard two-matrix factorization, and a refinement/distillation phase to recover quality. It can fail because evidence is limited to Skip-gram word2vec-style embeddings on analogy and similarity benchmarks, so gains may not transfer to large transformer embedding tables, and KAN function evaluation may erode the latency and memory savings the compression was meant to provide.
rationale: The method is cheap to implement and fits constrained infrastructure, but it is validated only on Skip-gram word embeddings, so its benefit for production-scale LLM embedding tables requires workload-specific validation.

claims.statement: It replaces the purely linear low-rank decomposition of an embedding matrix with a factorization that inserts learnable univariate (KAN-style) nonlinear projections inside the compressed embedding layer, optionally initialized from a pretrained uncompressed embedding and refined with distillation. The cost is additional per-parameter compute for the learnable univariate functions, extra implementation complexity over a standard two-matrix factorization, and a refinement/distillation phase to recover quality. It can fail because evidence is limited to Skip-gram word2vec-style embeddings on analogy and similarity benchmarks, so gains may not transfer to large transformer embedding tables, and KAN function evaluation may erode the latency and memory savings the compression was meant to provide.

Under matched parameter budgets on Word Analogy and Semantic Similarity benchmarks, the KAN-augmented factorization produces more faithful compressed embeddings than a standard low-rank baseline; no multiplicative factor is reported in the abstract.
